preconditions.description: The number of words in the scroll is between 1 and 100,000 inclusive.
Each word in the scroll has at least one lowercase English letter.
The total length of all words in the scroll does not exceed 1,000,000.
The words are read from stdin, with the first line being the integer n and the subsequent lines being the words.

postconditions.description: The result is either 0 (no valid way to recover the original scroll) or a non-negative integer modulo 10^9+7.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= i < n for i in range(n))
postconditions.description: The indices of words are valid (0-based, within bounds).

postconditions.expression: all(len(candidate) == len(word) - 1 or len(candidate) == len(word) for candidate in candidates)
postconditions.description: For each word, a candidate is either the original word (no deletion) or a word with exactly one letter deleted.

postconditions.expression: all(candidate <= word for candidate in candidates)
postconditions.description: For each word, a candidate is lexicographically less than or equal to the original word (if deletion is applied).

postconditions.expression: all(candidates[i] <= candidates[i+1] for i in range(n-1))
postconditions.description: The sequence of candidates (after deletions) is lexicographically non-decreasing.
The result is the count of all valid candidate sequences (mod 10^9+7), where each sequence is a possible way to recover the original scroll by deleting at most one letter from each word.
